title: Show the winner as 'not yet established', with the number that would establish it
problem: The lab can rank four strategies, but the intervals overlap and none survives the multiplicity adjustment. A leaderboard that shows a rank invites the reader to act on noise.
paths: (a) Show no rank at all until the threshold is met. (b) Show the rank with the interval and the required-n column beside it. (c) Show the rank and a 'significant' badge.
recommendation: Path (b). It answers the user's question honestly - who is ahead, by how much, and how little that means - without hiding the ordering or implying it is real.
risk: A reader still screenshots the top row out of context; mitigate with the required-n column in the same row, not a footnote.

title: Make dispersion a first-class published column, not a diagnostic
problem: Under-dispersion (0.26-0.58) is the mechanical reason no line is bettable, and it is invisible on the current site.
paths: (a) Leave it in the lab only. (b) Publish it beside every originated line, with a one-line reading guide. (c) Add a hard gate that blocks publishing a line whose dispersion is below a set threshold.
recommendation: Path (b) now, path (c) only after the shrinkage is re-fitted - a gate on a number we cannot yet improve would block the site rather than the model.
cost: Low: one column and one sentence.
risk: A threshold set from 132 games would be arbitrary; do not pretend it is a league standard.

title: Retire the totals leg to 'league mean plus nothing' until signal exists
problem: Predicted total versus actual total correlates at -0.03, and a control that ignores the teams beats every strategy on total MAE.
paths: (a) Keep publishing a model total. (b) Publish 'league mean' as the total with the model's deviation shown separately as an unvalidated opinion. (c) Stop publishing totals.
recommendation: Path (b). It keeps the two-estimator comparison alive (R051), states plainly that the total is the control, and stops a weak number being presented as a model output.
risk: Readers may read 'league mean' as a prediction; label it as the control that won.

title: Fix the scheduled availability capture before adding any availability feature
problem: The one workflow that would create a legal point-in-time record has never had a successful run; its 2026-11-17 run failed. Without it every availability feature is untestable.
paths: (a) Build more availability features now. (b) Repair the capture workflow first and prove one clean week. (c) Drop availability from the model.
recommendation: Path (b). It is the cheapest item on this page and it unblocks four other requirements at once.
cost: One workflow repair and one week of waiting.
risk: The official page may change structure mid-week; the workflow's drift check already fails loudly rather than storing garbage - keep that behaviour.

title: Publish the Week 11 slate now, with the market columns blank
problem: The forecast is only prospective if it exists before kickoff. Week 11 has no injury report yet, so a forecast made today is a legal (if uninformed) pre-kickoff registration.
paths: (a) Wait for the injury report. (b) Publish now with the report-dependent features explicitly absent, and re-issue a second registration when the report lands. (c) Publish one forecast after the report and call it pre-kickoff.
recommendation: Path (b). Two dated registrations are stronger evidence than one, and the diff between them is the injury signal - which is exactly the surprise the brief asks for.
cost: Already produced by this session's build.
risk: Two registrations can be cherry-picked later; publish both and forbid deleting either.

title: Make the multiplicity count a committed number, not a post-hoc one
problem: Every extra strategy searched increases the chance that the best one is luck. The lab declares 12 comparisons today; a future session could add arms and quietly change the threshold.
paths: (a) Document the rule only. (b) Freeze the arm list in a file the build reads, and fail the build if it changes without a version bump.
recommendation: Path (b). It is a five-line guard and it is the difference between a pre-registration and a story.
cost: Small: one JSON field and one check in the verifier.
risk: Genuinely new ideas become awkward to add - that is the point; they require a new registration window.

title: Separate 'signal' and 'staking' on every leaderboard row, and leave staking empty
problem: A lucky staking run can mask a bad signal; the brief says so and the repo agrees. But there is no price, so only the signal column can be filled.
paths: (a) Fill staking with a reference-market price from a third party. (b) Leave staking blank with 'no licensed price' in every cell. (c) Compute a hypothetical ROI at a made-up price.
recommendation: Path (b). Path (a) imports an unlicensed number into a column the site will later compare against licensed data; path (c) is fabrication.
cost: None: the column exists and is already empty.
risk: A permanently empty column looks broken; the header must carry the reason, not a tooltip.

title: Put the required sample size next to every ranking
problem: The honest answer to 'who is winning' is 'nobody can be winning yet, here is how many games it would take'.
paths: (a) State it in prose on the methodology page. (b) Print it in the ranking table header with the arithmetic shown. (c) Omit it.
recommendation: Path (b). It converts an opinion about sample size into an arithmetic claim the reader can check.
risk: The power calculation depends on assumptions about the true effect; show the sensitivity, not a single number.

title: Consolidate the six subsites behind one entry point instead of adding a seventh
problem: This repository publishes six dashboards for one brief. Each has unique data and each contradicts another on at least one number.
paths: (a) Add this page as a seventh subsite. (b) Make the root page the only entry point and label the others as archives with a date and a known-defects note. (c) Delete the redundant ones.
recommendation: Path (b). Nothing is discarded, the contradiction is disclosed, and the reader is not asked to choose between six sites.
risk: Archive labels can be read as endorsement; each archive needs its own 'what is wrong with this' line.

title: Add an injury/personnel ablation harness rather than penalty weights
problem: The brief asks for ablations, not fixed penalties. The repo's model still ships position penalty weights that were never validated (QB 2.6 points, WR 0.55, and so on).
paths: (a) Tune the weights on 148 games. (b) Run the same model with and without a personnel block and report the paired difference with an interval. (c) Drop personnel entirely.
recommendation: Path (b). It is the only version that can answer 'does this feature help' without fitting the answer into the weights; and on 148 games it will very probably report 'no measurable difference', which is a useful result rather than a failure.
cost: Needs a verified availability input, so it is gated on SC-04.
risk: An ablation with null results may be read as 'the feature is useless' when the real answer is 'the sample is too small'.
